title: There Are Only 3 Problems In Life
author: Jeff Matlow
source: The Best Leadership Newsletter Ever, July 20, 2026
summary: Jeff Matlow proposes a diagnostic framework that reduces every leadership and life problem to one of three categories: head, heart, or bank account. Head problems are intellectual challenges—confusion, decision paralysis, ego, the tendency to over-analyze—that create more confusion than clarity. Heart problems are emotional burdens—resentment, fear, imposter syndrome, the need for approval—that cause leaders to avoid accountability conversations and take everything personally. Bank account problems are resource constraints, real or imagined, but Matlow argues they are often used as convenient scapegoats for what are actually head or heart problems. The diagnostic power of this framework is that most leaders waste months solving the wrong problem: throwing money at an ego issue, reading leadership books when they should be setting boundaries, calling something a resource problem when it is actually a courage problem. The faster a leader correctly identifies which category their problem belongs to, the faster they can move toward resolution rather than motion.

From the archives… Every once in a while I reread an old article and realize it’s more relevant today than when I wrote it.
And if you’re ready to change your trajectory, this is the last chance to get into the free Leadership Diagnostic Workshop.
I don’t care how complex or unique you think your difficulties are - what I’m telling you is that they can all be boiled down to one of three problems: Your head Your heart, or Your bank account.

The question isn’t whether you have this type of problem - the question is how much the problems in your head are limiting you from being the person you want to be and doing the things you want to do.
Here’s what I mean: Do you ever doubt yourself or identify with imposter syndrome?
Have you ever struggled with decision-making - or avoided tough conversations?
They manifest themselves as things like confusion, decision paralysis, and/or a desperate need to be right.
